serial_location: back, right side, under the Turned Pro line
serial_appearance: gold metallic foil stamp, raised, catches the light
checklist_number_on_card: R2 (printed in the design, top-left corner)
why: genuine numbered card, but 71 of 150 is neither the first nor the last of the run

checklist_number_on_card: 162 (flat printed ink, top centre) -- NOT a serial
why: genuine numbered card; 7 of 15 is mid-run. The printed 162 is the checklist number and must never be read as a serial

serial_location: front, lower-left, above the name plate
serial_appearance: gold metallic foil stamp on a refractor surface; photo is a tight crop at an angle
why: genuine numbered card and the last of a 15-card run -- a bookend

number_on_card: 1 of 2000 -- flat printed ink at the bottom right, no metallic texture
other_numbers_in_photo: PSA certificate number 148801592, barcode and QR code on the slab label -- none of these are serials
why: '1 of 2000' is the set's print-run statement, printed identically on every card in the run; it is not a serial and this is not card #1. The tell is the printing: flat ink with no metallic texture. A title reading '1/2000' or '1 of 2000' must not be taken as a bookend.

set: 2010 Ace Authentic Aces Dual Autographs, PSA/DNA-slabbed, sold at auction
number_on_card: 7 OF 25 -- flat printed in a box, bottom-left; not a foil stamp
autograph: two signatures in ink directly on the card surface (on-card), not on a sticker
other_numbers_in_photo: PSA/DNA cert 86644708 on the slab label
why: Ace Authentic could not produce on-card autographs, so any Ace Authentic card with a signature on the card itself is a fake -- even hand-numbered, even slabbed and certified, even sold at auction. Separately, the '7 OF 25' is flat print, not a serial.

set: Ace Authentic, US Open design, in a top-loader
number_on_card: 8/10 -- hand-written on a round holographic Ace Authentic sticker in the bottom-right corner; not a foil stamp
autograph: one signature in ink directly on the card surface (on-card), across the photo
sticker: round holographic circle sticker carrying the Ace Authentic logo with the numbering written on it
why: Numbering on this type of round holographic circle sticker is fake: a genuine serial is a foil stamp on the card itself, never a number on a sticker. The on-card autograph is a second, independent reason to reject it (Ace Authentic could not produce on-card autos).

set: 2003 NetPro International Series, Court Authentic autograph RC #2C
serial_location: back, left edge, stamped vertically (reads bottom to top)
serial_appearance: dark stamp with little or no metallic sheen in the photo -- STILL a legitimate serial on old NetPro cards
autograph: the signature printed on the back is the NetPro president's certificate signature, not the player autograph; the player autograph is on the front
why: genuine numbered card. The stamp looks flat and dark rather than metallic, but on early NetPro (2003 Court Authentic) that is how the serial was applied, so the photo step must not reject it for lacking sheen. It is dropped only because 454 is mid-run and the run of 500 is not under the 500 limit.

set: 1991 NetPro Tour Star base card, bought back and stamped for NetPro's 20th anniversary; sealed in a case with a '20th NETPRO' seal and serial
serial_location: front, bottom-right corner of the photo
serial_appearance: gold metallic foil stamp -- the buyback numbering added on top of an unnumbered base card
why: A NetPro base card is normally excluded, but a buyback carries gold metallic foil numbering added by NetPro and is genuine and wanted. The tells: the gold foil stamp on the front and the '20th NETPRO' seal on the case. Listing text says buyback or 20th anniversary; the photo step can confirm the foil stamp.
